content.content:
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element.

2. Domain complete: the order-free claim ranges over every flag the form carries. The parent that fixes the extended form records the form's surface as one `-m <summary>`, repeated `--on <id>` and repeated `--evaluates <id>`; order-free recognition is a claim about exactly that surface. Fail if the dependent's account of what is recognized in any order covers a proper subset of those three — it enumerates `-m` and `--on` and stops, presents that pair as the form's flags, or otherwise leaves the recognition order of `--evaluates` unstated — or if the dependent gives no account of which flags the order-freedom covers at all; name the flag left out. A clause that speaks of the form's flags as a whole passes only if no enumeration narrows it: once the claim is elaborated by an enumeration, that enumeration must name all three, because an enumeration of two presented as the claim's extent leaves the third flag's recognition order unstated.

3. No order between flags: fail if any element requires one flag to precede or follow another — `--evaluates` must follow `--on` because placement is known before the checks are named, `--on` must come first, `-m` must come first or last, occurrences of either repeated kind must be contiguous, one repeated kind's occurrences must finish before the other's begin, or the invocation must be grouped or normalized before recognition. Fail equally if the order-freedom is weakened: permitted rather than required, holding only for some invocations (only when the ids resolve, only when no other argument intervenes, only up to some point in the invocation), or if an order-dependent refusal is admitted — the same arguments accepted in one arrangement and refused in another. Name the pair, the qualifier or the refusal, and the clause that carries it.

4. No scan boundary: fail if an element makes a named flag's being recognized depend on its position through a termination or boundary rule — recognition stops at the first argument the form does not name, at the first bare word, at the first argument that is not an option, at a `--` separator, or at a fixed positional slot — for then whether a `--on` or `--evaluates` occurrence after that boundary counts turns on where it sits, which is an order. Name the rule and the flag it strands. Refusing an unnamed argument is the form's own refusal decision and not this clause's; the dependent neither has to nor may decide it here, so silence about unnamed arguments is not itself a failure.

5. The flags themselves are not re-decided: the flag set, each flag's requiredness and repeatability, what `--evaluates` lands and how an id is resolved are fixed by the parents, and order-free recognition must not reopen them. Fail if an element makes the count or effect of a repeated flag depend on where its occurrences sit (an occurrence honoured only if first or last, a repeatable flag collapsed to one when its occurrences are not adjacent), or if it makes `--evaluates` required or single, gives it an effect besides the evaluates edges of the node being born, resolves its ids through `--on`'s resolution, or relaxes `-m`'s singleness or `--on`'s requiredness; name the clause and the fixed part it reopens.
content.rationale: Flag recognition is where the form's named parts meet the birth; the gate keeps the use sound without testing the parse itself. Both nodes are requirement sentences, so the cell is the matrix default — the gate plus a flag to extend the matrix. The former single license line no longer covers the use: the form whose recognition this dependent orders now carries three parts, not two, and a license-only check cannot tell a requirement that ranges over all three from one whose enumeration stops at `-m` and `--on`, nor one that fixes no order from one that fixes an order in a single clause. The criteria therefore decide the order claim in both directions at once — the domain of the claim (every flag the parent records on the form) and its freedom (no pair of flags ordered, no scan boundary, no grouping or normalisation, no qualifier narrowing it) — while leaving the flag set, requiredness, repeatability, landing and id resolution to the parents that fix them. Naming the three flags names the form's recorded surface, not the dependent's spelling, so the criterion survives a rewording that decides the same thing. Nothing is executed for this form: a reviewer applies the criteria to the recorded dependent and its recorded prerequisite.
